title: Concurrent Spatial and Channel 'Squeeze & Excitation' in Fully Convolutional Networks
grouping: Four panels, each with a centred caption underneath: (a) a small top-left panel showing where the blocks go in the network, (b) and (c) the two single attention blocks, and (d), the largest, bottom-right, combining them. A notation legend sits in a grey-filled box at the bottom left (convolution symbol, ReLU glyph, global-pooling glyph, sigmoid). No panel frames.
shapes_depth: The input feature map U is a white 3-D wireframe cuboid labelled C, H, W. Outputs are 3-D cuboids whose faces are coloured to show the reweighting: channel excitation paints vertical slices in different tints (peach, green, orange), spatial excitation paints a 2 x 2 quadrant pattern (blue, yellow, red, green), the combined block shows both. Squeezed vectors are thin tall white bars with a coloured excitation bar beside them; the spatial map is a flat 2 x 2 coloured square. Operators are circled x and +; convolutions are written as a star with kernel and channel sub/superscripts. In (a) the network is a mini U of flat pale-blue bars with a peach bottleneck, and the inserted blocks are red bars, joined to the plain version by a thick green arrow labelled 'Insert SE blocks'.
proposed_highlight: The new blocks are red in the placement panel (a), the only saturated element there. In the detail panels the effect of each block is shown by colour on its output cuboid rather than by highlighting the block.
lesson: Show what an attention block reweights by colouring its output cuboid - per-channel slices in different tints for channel attention, a 2 x 2 coloured quadrant pattern for spatial attention, both on the combined block - against a plain white input cuboid.
notes: Venue from Semantic Scholar. Panel (a) is a small placement sketch; the rest of the figure is module internals, hence module-detail. The figure is embedded in the PDF as one raster image, so photo_share is unknown (null) and the palette is measured over the whole raster.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: panel (d) stacks the spatial-excitation branch (top) and the channel-excitation branch (bottom) from one input cube U, each redrawn exactly as in panels (c) and (b), and joins their recalibrated cubes at a circled + into Û_scSE

relations.form: (b) cSE and (c) sSE as separate panels, each from a white cube U to a recalibrated cube, captioned with their names
in (d) the two branches split from U, each multiplies U at a circled x, and curved arrows bring both outputs to a circled + 'Add'

feature maps are 3-D cubes with C, H, W edges; channel recalibration colours the cube in vertical slices along C, spatial recalibration colours it in quadrants over H x W, and the combined cube shows both
within each branch: global pooling glyph or 1x1 conv -> thin vectors z (C, C/2, C) or map q -> σ -> x with U
(a) a before/after pair of small U-shaped F-CNN schematics joined by a green arrow 'Insert SE blocks after every encoder & decoder block', the inserted blocks drawn as red bars

channels.colour: in the cubes, colour = excitation weights (slice colours for channel, quadrant colours for spatial); in (a), blue = encoder/decoder, peach = bottleneck, red = SE block; peach also fills the Û_cSE cube's front face, so peach carries two unrelated meanings
channels.shape: cubes = feature tensors, thin bars = channel vectors, small grids = spatial maps, circled x/+ = recalibration and addition
channels.line: solid arrows; operator symbols (⋆ conv, σ) are labels on the arrows, keyed in a legend box
channels.frame: only the legend box is framed; panels separated by whitespace and captions

quality.strengths: the tensors are drawn and recalibration is shown by how the output cube is coloured (slices vs quadrants vs both), so what each block changes is visible; (d) reuses the (b) and (c) drawings so the combination reads by recognition
quality.weaknesses: the four panels sit on an irregular grid ((b) top right, (c) mid left, (d) bottom right) with the legend in the remaining corner; panel (a) uses a separate colour code; operator notation like ⋆^{C/2}_{1x1} is typeset on small arrows

insights.structure: Four captioned panels in a 2 x 2 grid: (a) a small top-left schematic of the encoder-decoder before and after inserting red SE blocks, (b) cSE and (c) sSE as single-path blocks, and (d) the largest, bottom-right, stacking sSE above cSE and summing them.
insights.data: The input U is a white wireframe cuboid labelled C, H, W, and each output is a cuboid whose faces are tinted to show the reweighting: vertical coloured slices for channel excitation, a 2 x 2 quadrant of blue/yellow/red/green for spatial excitation, both on the scSE output.
insights.emphasis: The colour of the output cuboids makes the difference between channel and spatial recalibration visible at a glance, and the combined block in (d) is the largest panel.
insights.flow: Left to right in each panel: U branches into a squeeze path (thin bars or a 2 x 2 map with sigma) and a skip that meets it at a circled x, then a circled + in (d) merges the two recalibrated cuboids.
insights.avoid: The panel captions mislabel the blocks ('Spatial Squeeze and Channel Excitation (cSE)' and the scSE caption repeats 'Channel Excitation'), and the grey notation legend is wedged into the bottom-left corner; check captions against the method and give the legend its own row.

arrangement.units: four unframed panels each with a centred caption below; a grey-filled notation box at bottom left
arrangement.inputs_as: a white 3-D wireframe feature cuboid U (C x H x W)
arrangement.shared: the same U cuboid and the same squeeze glyphs recur across panels (b)-(d)
